description: Stereo recorder that cuts what it captures into slices at transients and plays them back at any speed in either direction, up to eight voices at once, with a feedback loop and a three-band equaliser

params.text: Chooses which slice is played, sweeping across the slices found in the recording from the first to the last
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the scan jack, -1 to +1
Sets the level a peak has to reach before it is counted as the start of a new slice, 0V to 10V; moving it rescans the recording
Sets how close together two slice points are allowed to be, 1ms to 1 second; moving it rescans the recording
While it is held down the module slides every knob picked on the menu to a new random setting, and back when it is let go
Sets how much of the output is fed back into the buffer, 0 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the feedback jack, -1 to +1
Lifts or cuts everything below 80Hz in the output, -12dB to +12dB
Lifts or cuts a band around 2500Hz in the output, -12dB to +12dB
Lifts or cuts everything above 12000Hz in the output, -12dB to +12dB
Sets the playback speed: eight times over backwards at the bottom of its travel, halted a quarter of the way up, normal speed at halfway and eight times over forwards at the top
Sets how many voices play the recording at once, 1 to 8; above one they are spread across the stereo field
Sets how long the sample-and-hold takes to slide to each new value, 0 to 1 second
Multiplies the sample-and-hold output, 0 to 5 times
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the amount jack, -1 to +1
Sets how often the sample-and-hold takes a new value, 0.01Hz to 100Hz
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the rate jack, -1 to +1
Starts and stops recording into the buffer
Cycles the transport: each press moves between looping and playing once through
Stops playback at once; held down for two seconds it also empties the buffer and its slices

inputs.text: The left side of the signal being recorded; with nothing patched to the right jack this one feeds both sides
The right side of the signal being recorded
Added to the SCAN knob through the trimmer below it, a tenth of the sweep per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the THRSH knob through the trimmer below it, one volt of threshold per volt
Added to the FDBK knob through the trimmer below it, a tenth per volt; the total is held between 0 and 1
Added to the SPEED knob, one times speed per volt; the total is held between eight times backwards and eight times forwards
Added to the POLY knob, seven tenths of a voice per volt; the total is held between 1 and 8
Added to the AMT knob through the trimmer below it, half a step per volt; the total is held between 0 and 5
Added to the RATE knob through the trimmer below it, one volt per doubling of the rate; the total is held between 0.01Hz and 100Hz
Replaces the left side of the output entirely with whatever is patched here, before the equaliser
Replaces the right side of the output entirely with whatever is patched here, before the equaliser
A rising edge starts and stops recording into the buffer
A rising edge cycles the transport between looping and playing once through
Held above 0.5V it stops playback, and held there for two seconds it empties the buffer and its slices
While it is held above 1V the module slides every knob picked on the menu to a new random setting

outputs.text: The left side of the recording as it is played back, through the return, the equaliser and the feedback loop
The right side of the recording as it is played back, through the return, the equaliser and the feedback loop
The sample-and-hold, ±10V, taken from the module's own feedback signal and slewed
The left side of the output before the equaliser, for sending to an effect
The right side of the output before the equaliser, for sending to an effect

notes: the module does nothing until something is recorded into it. Press REC with a signal at the input jacks, press it again to stop, then press PLAY/LOOP.
the blue line across the waveform display is the loop end point and is moved by dragging it. It is a parameter with no knob of its own, so a click on it cannot reach this help.
slices are found by scanning the recording for peaks above the threshold, no closer together than the minimum slice time. Moving either control rescans the whole recording.
a cable in either return jack replaces that side of the output outright rather than being mixed with it, so the send and return pair is an insert, not an aux.
menu: Load WAV — reads a WAV file into the buffer in place of anything recorded
Save WAV — writes whatever is in the buffer out as a WAV file
Morph Time — a slider setting how long the CHAOS button takes to slide the knobs to their random settings
Morph Amount — a slider setting how far from their current settings the CHAOS button is allowed to move them
Morph Targets — a tick for each knob the CHAOS button is allowed to move: EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Threshold, Min Slice Time, Scan, Feedback, S&H Slew, S&H Amount, S&H Rate and Speed
